context:
Buddies roam one named area at a time, and the areas the map files provide are often too big, so the plan is to cut each into smaller areas drawn as polygons, which are flat outlines given by a list of corner points. An AI model would draw them, looking at what a person would: the zone's map and minimap, a top-down picture, pictures of cliffs and lake shores, one picture per quest with its spawn points and regions laid over the ground, a database lookup on any creature's spawn point, and the area's wiki page. The unsettled part is how that runs: the model could draw one zone at a time, offline, with each drawing checked in a view of the zone from above before it is kept, which keeps bad outlines out but costs a human review per zone. The pictures themselves could come from the custom game client, which can render a scene to an image without opening a window, or from the project's own zone-view renderer, which already draws terrain from above for that review.

Every starting valley would be split into two or three areas, and every other zone too, using the kinds of monster living in each part (boars here, scorpions there, demons elsewhere) as the clue to where one area ends. In a town, including the plains round it, a buddy would pick its next target as whatever is nearest, either a monster to fight or a friendly townsperson to talk to, so it mostly fights and sometimes talks. How often "sometimes" happens is a number still to pick, for instance one target in five being a townsperson: a higher share makes towns livelier but slows the fighting. Buddies also have errands in towns, such as visiting a trainer, a vendor or a repairer, and the open point is whether a due errand still goes ahead of the nearest-target rule or becomes one more thing in the mix.

Separately, towns are already marked by hand-placed circles, inside which buddies do town things like errands and leisure instead of fighting. A drawn area carrying the nearest-target rule overlaps the circle on the Valley of Trials' town side, so either the drawn area's rule takes over inside the circle, letting buddies fight there, or the circle keeps meaning errands first and the rule applies only in the rest of the area.

Last, where an area has almost no monsters and almost no friendly people, buddies would not roam but would follow their player, spread along an arc around them. For that, "almost none" needs a measure, such as the spawns inside the area divided by its size in square yards and compared with a threshold. The count could be taken once when the area is drawn, which is cheap and stable but blind to later changes, or live, which tracks what is actually alive near the player but costs work each time and can make buddies flip between roaming and the arc.
